title: Marked polygon correlations and one-arc bounds
main_claim: At the critical honeycomb activity rho_v=(2+sqrt2)^{-1/2}, the squared-length polygon mass sum over translation classes with diam P <= H of rho_v^{|P|}|P|^2 is at most C_eta H^{2/3+eta}. This comes from a sharp two-mark cylinder bound log C(p,p') <= -4/3 log s + 617/1200 log(b/s) + o(log b). The paper also proves a polynomial one-arc bound A(p,p') <= b^C that holds even for arbitrarily unequal walls.

issues.location: Sec 5 (05_analysis.tex): Prop. sharp trial estimate, Prop. transport (implementation of trial actions), Lemma localization; Thm 4 real-energy coercivity (04_mean.tex)
issues.description: These analytic steps are written in very compressed form: the smoothing errors, the curved-contour residual kernels, the transport implementation of the imaginary trial fields, and the source and quadratic estimates adapted from the Electric companion (Thm 4.3, Lemma 5.2). I could not check them line by line. I found no specific step that fails, so this is not a located gap, but correctness rests on these sketches and on companion inputs I did not re-check.

coverage:
I read all of Secs 1-3, Sec 5 (trial actions, the mark-selection lemma, the determinant lemma, the final theorem and its deduction), Sec 6 (the one-arc identity statement and the full proof of the bound), and the key statements of Sec 4. I skimmed the transport, source and quadratic propositions and the coercivity proof. Checks I ran with sympy/mpmath:
- Residues of F_s and E_s at i*sigma*beta, and F_s(2i*sigma*beta).
- The fused double identities E_s(v)E_s(v+i beta) and E_c(v)E_c(v+i beta).
- r_1 and r_2, the string-count identity (2d)^n prod r = (2c)^{sum l^2}, F(2 lambda)=(2c)^2/2, and the sign identity (-1)^{sb-M^2}=(-1)^{sb+M}.
- Denominator: the integral of S equals 5pi^2/(72 beta), giving 5/24 log N; the Cauchy/sech interpolation identity G=K(z-w)(1-B(z)B(w)) (numerical); the trace-limit Fourier bookkeeping.
- Legendre mass J_n: exact at n=2, and the -1/4 log n asymptotic.
- C_* identity (2d)C_*/a_* = gamma/2, and rho-hat = 1/c_*.
- Determinant symbols sqrt det T_inf and the shoulder symbol in y-form; log integrals -7pi^2/48 and -5pi^2/48, giving 7gamma/8 and 5gamma/16.
- Shoulder activity sum 0.429757 < 0.44; the self-cost inequality 4x(2cosh x-1)cosh^2x cosh^2(x/2)(1+4x^2) <= sinh4x cosh3x and the resulting -2/(1+4x^2) bracket; common gain 6 beta A0 - kappa A0^2 = 1.
- Final exponent assembly: -16/9 L_X + 0.68556(L_Y-L_X), i.e. -4/3 log s + 617/1200 log(b/s).
- The polygon deduction: the D^{4/3} short cutoff via the D^{-2} tail; the retained-pair fraction (D^{9/8} excluded vs |P|>D^{4/3}); the margins c1<1/2 and c4<gamma/8; t>=1/2 via rotation/reflection; injective projection since |T|>2D; O(S^2) setups times S^{-4/3}(D/S)^{2/3} = D^{2/3}; the dyadic sum.
- The compactness argument that removes the wall-ratio restriction in the one-arc theorem.

Their checks overlap with this paper: the same determinant symbol (-7pi^2/48), the denominator integral 5pi^2/(72b), the Legendre mass n^{-1/4}, the 5/24 coefficient, and the 1/(2 gamma kappa) style constants. That agreement supports the shared inputs, and I re-verified them independently here. Nothing on the board pointed to a shared lemma failure.
